mechanics: Hold Up rotates the dolphin's nose upward, hold Down rotates it downward
Rotation is continuous with no angle limits — full flips, reversal at any time, chained rotations while airborne

Momentum is the core mechanic: every action builds, preserves or loses speed, with no boost buttons or power-ups
Water behaves elastically like a trampoline — perfect entries preserve and convert momentum, poor entries create drag and large speed loss
No swim button; swimming is driven entirely by physics and body orientation
Surface grinding / hydroplaning at shallow angle and sufficient speed, with light springy bounces and spray, failing when speed drops
Launch height depends on speed, entry angle, exit angle and timing

Speed feedback: narrower longer spray, extended foam trails, rising wind noise, heavier entry sounds, more exaggerated animation
Constant idle animation — tail movement, body flex, anticipation poses, even airborne
Scoring rewards maximum altitude, longest airtime, top speed, longest grind distance, flips performed and momentum combos
Combo system rewards alternating smoothly between underwater swimming, surface grinding and aerial movement
notes: No genre in the index fits an arcade momentum-trick game; classified None and built from no-genre rather than forcing Sports, whose bounded field and directed range both contradict an endless ocean.
Volumetric play space: the player swims below the surface and flies above it. Treated as a play-height envelope over one representable water surface, so CHECK rather than a real occlusion problem.
The entire build is one water surface plus sky. There is no obstacle geometry to place, by the prompt's own instruction that the ocean carries no obstacles.

notes_for_us: The genre index has no home for a physics-momentum trick game. Sports says 'physics-based athletics' in its one-line description, which pulls this way, but both its shapes are a bounded field or a directed range with a target, and every option is a boundary, a start position or a scoring volume. Taking it would have produced a court on an ocean.

The whole play surface of this game is water, and the only handle for water is `water-body`, a universal environment option written as 'a lake, river, sea, or pool — whether swum through or treated as a barrier'. The surface the game is entirely played on therefore arrives downstream as scenery, and its elastic/grindable behaviour has nowhere to attach.

Scale is close to meaningless for a featureless endless ocean — every band builds the same picture — but the field is mandatory and there is no way to say 'this axis does not apply here', so the record carries an assumption that reads more load-bearing than it is.

No-genre's axes give `volumetric` for swimming and flight, which is right, but this prompt's volume is exactly the benign case the note describes (one surface, envelope above and below). Emitting bare CHECK loses that distinction, and `notes` was the only place to say so.

All four were rejected and the prompt is unambiguously a real, shipped game concept.

'Ten maps' collides with the segments rule. Nothing in the network holds a between-rounds map-selection device, and it is a common Roblox pattern (spinner, wheel, vote board). It is visible geometry with a functional role, so it reads as a Tracker-family option that does not exist.

notes_for_us: The player being a cat invalidates the spatial baseline the whole system is built on. Part I's 4-stud avatar, 11-stud jump and 16-stud walk speed are what every gap, corridor and platform figure derives from, and a cat is none of them. Nothing in the handoff can say 'scale the traversable geometry to a small animal', so it went in as a free-text image line where no measurement step will read it.

Survival's shape list has no city. `space-bounded` was taken because it is the default and the prompt does not contradict it, but the honest fit was `traversal-city` from the catalogue — and reaching for it would have meant inventing the rooftops the prompt never mentioned. Silence pushed the build to the blander shape, correctly by the rules, and the enriched expansion then invented exactly the thing the rules forbade.

Choosing Resource Survival meant taking `buildzone-plot`, which the prompt's own protagonist rules out. The brief's instruction to keep it makes the conflict visible, but the emitted image list now asks for buildable shelter ground on a cat game with nothing in the block marking it as rejected.
